title: Constructed exact transport of inverse-image constant module coefficients
statement: Let g:Y→X be a scheme morphism and B a commutative ring in the site universe. Inverse image of the constant B-ring is canonically isomorphic to the constant ring on Y. Transport to the AsSmall model and restrict the scalar action along the inverse of this comparison and the canonical constant-sheaf site comparison. This gives the explicitly defined functor relativeFiniteModelModules from modules over g⁻¹(B_X) to modules over the actual constant B-ring on the model site. It is an additive equivalence. Its induced functor on the standard derived localizations commutes with homology. No module objects are selected from an existence theorem.

proof.text: The constant-ring inverse-image map is the comparison of two left adjoints to global sections. Identify its adjunct with the constant-presheaf sheafification unit; uniqueness of left adjoints makes the map invertible.

proof.text: Compose the inverse constant-sheaf comparison for AsSmall with transport of the inverse constant-ring map. Define the module functor by precomposition and scalar restriction along this actual ring isomorphism.

proof.text: The pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence construction provides inverses both to precomposition and to restriction along a ring isomorphism. Their composite is an equivalence, and addition of maps is sectionwise. Apply mapDerivedCategory and mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso to this exact additive functor.
